newsitem.title: MEXICO: U.S. drugs czar has doubts about "certification".
newsitem.headline: U.S. drugs czar has doubts about "certification".

text.p: U.S. drugs czar Barry McCaffrey said on Tuesday he had doubts about the "certification" process under which Washington grades the anti-narcotics efforts of other countries.
Asked in an interview with Mexican pro-government TV channel 24 Horas whether certification was a valid process, McCaffrey replied, speaking Spanish:

"We should study this process, and we should also remember that we have to work together, Mexico, the United States and all the countries in the hemisphere. It is a common problem and we should work as equals."
Switching to English, McCaffrey said the recent arrest of his Mexican counterpart, Gen. Jesus Gutierrez Rebollo, on drugs corruption charges was "an enormous embarrassment."

He declined to say what recommendation he would give President Bill Clinton on Mexico but said he fully supported President Ernesto Zedillo's anti-narcotics efforts and praised the Mexican armed forces for their work against drug-trafficking.
Clinton must decide by the end of the month whether to "certify" Mexico as a country that is cooperating with the United States in its war on illegal drugs.
Countries that fail the test may face U.S. sanctions.
McCaffrey said both production and consumption of illegal drugs was a problem in the United States, and the same was true of Latin America.

Although it is a major consumer nation the United States also produces marijuana and methampetamines or "speed," he said, while cities in Latin American nations known for drug production such as Bogota and Lima also have serious drug consumption problems.
